title: Cap. VII: Junius — reprobationis vocabulum trifariam sumitur
latin: Atque hic notandum est, Reprobationis vocabulum apud Theologos trifariam sumi, ut recte a doctissimo Junio est observatum. Primo sumitur pro praeteritione et damnatione conjunctim: Et hoc sensu reprobi appellantur, non ex eo solummodo quod Deus decreverit gratiam efficacem illis negare, atque sic permittere ut a fine beatitudinis deficiant, sed quod insuper eos ad aeternas poenas destinaverit.
pass_a: And here it is to be noted that the vocabulary of Reprobation is taken among Theologians in three ways, as has been rightly observed by the most learned Junius. First it is taken for passing by and damnation jointly: And in this sense they are called reprobate, not from this alone that God has decreed to deny them efficacious grace, and so to permit that they fall short of the end of beatitude, but that moreover he has destined them to eternal punishments.
pass_b: Note here: among theologians the word reprobation is taken three ways, as the learned Junius rightly observed. First: for passing by and damnation jointly. In that sense people are called reprobate not only because God decreed to deny them efficacious grace and so permit them to fall short of beatitude's end, but also because he destined them to eternal punishments.

lemmas.gloss: first sense: passing by + damnation together

title: Cap. VII: first sense — antecedents of predamnation are not always antecedents of praeterition
latin: Qui sub unico vocabulo reprobandi ambos hosce actus Divinae voluntatis praetereundi et damnandi conjunctim includunt, vix poterunt aliquid certi de reprobatione affirmare. Nam quod est antecedaneum ad actum praedamnandi, non erit semper antecedaneum ad actum praetereundi: quod habet rationem causae motivae ad praedamnationem, non habebit illico naturam causae motivae aut demeriti causantis ad praeteritionem.
pass_a: Those who under the single vocabulary of reprobating include jointly both these acts of the Divine will of passing by and of damning, will scarcely be able to affirm anything certain concerning reprobation. For what is antecedent to the act of predamning will not always be antecedent to the act of passing by: what has the reason of a moving cause unto predamnation will not immediately have the nature of a moving cause or of demerit causing unto passing by.
pass_b: Those who under one word of reprobating join both divine acts — passing by and damning — can hardly affirm anything certain about reprobation. What precedes the act of predamning is not always what precedes the act of passing by: what moves as cause toward predamnation does not at once have the nature of a moving cause or demerit causing toward praeterition.

lemmas.gloss: antecedents of the two acts differ
moving cause toward predamnation not toward praeterition

title: Cap. VII: second and third senses — damnation alone; strict praeterition as non-election
latin: Secundo sumitur vocabulum reprobationis a nonnullis pro solo damnationis decreto: atque hoc sensu reprobari nihil aliud est quam aeternis cruciatibus destinari. Qui huic vocabulo nihil aliud inesse volunt quam destinationem ad poenas aeternas, in eo recte agunt, quod peccatum talis destinationis causam ponant; sed in eo labuntur, quod nihil altius in decreto electionis et rejectionis agnoscunt. Tertio igitur reprobationis vocabulum, qua est electioni contradictorie oppositum, sumitur pro sola praeteritione sive non-electione, atque innuit aeternam ordinationem in mente Divina negandi certis personis gratiam efficacem, et ad gloriam de facto perducentem. Potest autem talis reprobatio intelligi absque antecedaneo intuitu ad peccata rejectorum, tanquam causas motivas praedictae praeteritionis. Nam praesupposita tali praeteritione, tum demum praevidentur homines in peccato morituri et propter peccatum cruciandi. Deus igitur ab aeterno voluit hosce praeteritos, non-electos sive reprobatos addicere aeternis cruciatibus, non tamen quia praeteriti, sed quia mali et damnatione digni. Neque voluit eos punire in primo instanti rationis, in quo noluit glorificare, sed in illo altero, in quo illos consideravit ut peccatores a peccatis suis nunquam liberandos.
pass_a: Secondly the vocabulary of reprobation is taken by some for the decree of damnation alone: and in this sense to be reprobated is nothing other than to be destined to eternal torments. Those who will that nothing else be in this word than destination to eternal punishments do rightly in this, that they set sin as the cause of such destination; but they slip in this, that they acknowledge nothing higher in the decree of election and rejection. Thirdly therefore the vocabulary of reprobation, by which it is contradictorily opposite to election, is taken for passing by or non-election alone, and hints an eternal ordination in the Divine mind of denying to certain persons efficacious grace, and that which in fact leads to glory. But such reprobation can be understood without antecedent intuition toward the sins of the rejected, as moving causes of the aforesaid passing by. For such passing by being presupposed, then at last men are foresighted as about to die in sin and to be tormented on account of sin. God therefore from eternity willed to addict these passed-by, non-elect or reprobated ones to eternal torments, yet not because passed by, but because evil and worthy of damnation. Nor did he will to punish them in the first instant of reason, in which he was unwilling to glorify, but in that other, in which he considered them as sinners never to be freed from their sins.
pass_b: Second sense: some take reprobation for the damnation decree alone — to be reprobated is nothing but to be destined to eternal torments. Those who put only that in the word are right to set sin as cause of such destination; they slip in acknowledging nothing higher in the decree of election and rejection. Third sense: reprobation as contradictorily opposite to election is taken for praeterition or non-election alone — an eternal ordination in the divine mind to deny certain persons efficacious grace that in fact leads to glory. That reprobation can be understood without prior regard to the rejected's sins as moving causes of the passing by. Once such praeterition is presupposed, then at last men are foresighted as about to die in sin and be tormented for sin. From eternity God willed to addict these passed-by non-elect to eternal torments — not because passed by, but because evil and worthy of damnation. He did not will to punish them in the first instant of reason in which he refused to glorify, but in that other in which he considered them sinners never to be freed from their sins.

title: Cap. VII: our sum — praeterition from mere liberty; Paul and Judas
latin: Sententiae nostrae haec summa est: Praescientiam demeritorum non esse causam praeteritionis, non-electionis sive reprobationis stricte et proprie sumptae; sed sicuti ex mero Dei beneplacito dependet, quod certae quaedam personae per specialem providentiam, quam Praedestinationem appellamus, infallibiliter ordinentur ad gratiam et gloriam, ita ex mera Dei libertate dependet, quod aliae quaedam personae non ita ordinentur, sed a gratia hac efficaci destituantur, et a gloria deficere permittantur. Si quis ergo a nobis quaerat, cur Deus facillime et justissime potuerit tam Paulum quam Judam duritiae suae nativae relinquere, et aeternae miseriae addicere, qui etiam facillime potuit utrumque emollire, et ad aeternam gloriam perducere — si, inquam, quaeratur cur Judae non praeparaverit gratiam efficacem qua emolliretur et servaretur, Paulo praeparaverit; cur Judam non ordinaverit infallibiliter ad gloriam, Paulum ordinaverit — non confugimus ad praevisam fidem aut merita Pauli, neque ad praevisam Judae infidelitatem aut demerita, sed dicimus Deum misereri cujus vult emolliendo, et cujus vult minime misereri permissive indurando: Neque hujus tam diversae providentiae circa hasce personas aliam causam assignamus praeter Voluntatem Dei, quae est prima rectitudo. Atque sic habetis sententiam nostram.
pass_a: This is the sum of our opinion: that foresight of demerits is not the cause of passing by, non-election or reprobation strictly and properly taken; but as it hangs from the mere good pleasure of God that certain certain persons through special providence, which we call Predestination, are infallibly ordained unto grace and glory, so it hangs from the mere liberty of God that certain other persons are not so ordained, but are destitute of this efficacious grace, and are permitted to fall short of glory. If therefore anyone ask of us why God most easily and most justly could leave both Paul and Judas to their native hardness, and addict them to eternal misery, who also most easily could soften both, and lead them to eternal glory — if, I say, it be asked why he did not prepare for Judas efficacious grace by which he would be softened and saved, and did prepare it for Paul; why he did not ordain Judas infallibly unto glory, and did ordain Paul — we do not flee to the foresighted faith or merits of Paul, nor to the foresighted unbelief or demerits of Judas, but we say that God has mercy on whom he will by softening, and on whom he will he has mercy least by permissively hardening: Nor do we assign another cause of this so diverse providence concerning these persons besides the Will of God, which is the first rectitude. And so you have our opinion.
pass_b: Our sum: foresight of demerits is not the cause of praeterition, non-election, or reprobation strictly taken. As it hangs on mere good pleasure that certain persons by that special providence we call Predestination are infallibly ordained to grace and glory, so it hangs on mere divine liberty that others are not so ordained, but left without this efficacious grace and permitted to fall short of glory. If anyone asks why God could most easily and justly leave both Paul and Judas to native hardness and eternal misery — and could as easily soften both and lead them to eternal glory — why he prepared efficacious softening grace for Paul and not Judas, ordained Paul infallibly to glory and not Judas: we do not flee to Paul's foresighted faith or merits, nor Judas's foresighted unbelief or demerits. We say God has mercy on whom he will by softening, and on whom he will he has least mercy by permissive hardening. For providence so diverse about these persons we assign no cause but the Will of God, which is the first rectitude. So you have our opinion.

lemmas.gloss: praeterition hangs on mere divine liberty
no foresight faith/unbelief explains the difference

title: Cap. VII: opposing sententiae — Jesuits on foresight sins; Arminians on final unbelief
latin: Qui nobis adversantur e contra statuunt, Causam non-electionis sive reprobationis esse ea peccata in quibus reprobati praevidentur morituri. Atque haec est sententia quorundam Jesuitarum. Alii praevisam infidelitatem cum perseverantia finali in eadem dicunt esse causam reprobationis, ita ut nemo nisi in ipso mortis articulo consideretur a Deo ut reprobatus vel non-electus, idque propter hanc contumacem infidelitatem contra Deum evocantem. Atque haec sententia est Arminii et eorum quos Remonstrantes vocare solent.
pass_a: Those who are adverse to us establish on the contrary that the cause of non-election or reprobation is those sins in which the reprobate are foresighted as about to die. And this is the opinion of certain Jesuits. Others say that foresighted unbelief with final perseverance in the same is the cause of reprobation, so that no one except in the very article of death is considered by God as reprobated or non-elect, and that on account of this contumacious unbelief against God calling. And this is the opinion of Arminius and of those whom they are wont to call Remonstrants.
pass_b: Those against us hold the contrary: the cause of non-election or reprobation is the sins in which the reprobate are foresighted as about to die — so certain Jesuits. Others say foresighted unbelief with final perseverance in it is the cause, so that no one is considered by God reprobate or non-elect except in the very article of death, and that for contumacious unbelief against God calling. That is Arminius's view, and of those usually called Remonstrants.

title: Cap. VII close: same foundations — refute mixed, then confirm ours; Cap. VIII ahead
latin: Jam quibus argumentis hanc suam sententiam fulciant, qui hanc reprobationem sive praeteritionem a praevisis demeritis, vel infidelitate et perseverantia finali in eadem, arcessunt, audiamus. Neque opus est ut accurate distinguantur argumenta Jesuitarum et Arminianorum: nam iisdem plane fundamentis nituntur. Ut igitur inter legendum se nobis obtulerunt, ea mixtim proponemus. Hisce autem refutatis, ad sententiae nostrae confirmationem erit accedendum.
pass_a: Now by what arguments they prop up this their opinion, who fetch this reprobation or passing by from foresighted demerits, or from unbelief and final perseverance in the same, let us hear. Nor is there need that the arguments of the Jesuits and of the Arminians be accurately distinguished: for they rest on plainly the same foundations. As therefore they have offered themselves to us in reading, we will propose them mixed. But these having been refuted, it will be to be approached unto the confirmation of our opinion.
pass_b: Now let us hear by what arguments they prop this view — those who fetch reprobation or praeterition from foresighted demerits, or from unbelief and final perseverance in it. No need to split Jesuit and Arminian arguments carefully: they rest on plainly the same foundations. As they met us in reading, we will set them out mixed. Once refuted, we will turn to confirming our own opinion.

lemmas.gloss: Jesuit and Arminian arguments share foundations
